subject: Using terraclimate with NCEP data on a local directory

messages.author: 84b3cc0d6c62c03e
messages.subject: Using terraclimate with NCEP data on a local directory
parts:
Hello!

First, thank you for writing a great package and for cultivating such a helpful community. I'm trying to use NicheMapR to determine the thermal sensitivity of many anurans in the Southeast United States. I'm using NCEP data in a local directory to speed up the calculation of the microclimate models for 2011 to 2020. I would like to use the terraclimate climate change scenarios for 2011 to 2015 but am having difficulty running the microclimate model. I've gotten the models to work when I do not point the function to the local directory of NCEP data (i.e., the spatial argument is not used). The micro_ncep function does work and shows a difference in expected microclimates when the NCEP data is queried from the internet. Is it inappropriate to use the local directory to access NCEP data when implementing a climate change scenario? This error occurs even if a leap year is not chosen (I've checked 2011, 2012, 2014, and 2015) and after all the terra data is loaded. I've downloaded the most recent version of the package from GitHub (using devtools).

Code that runs into the error: 
m2<- micro_ncep(loc = c(-80.417778, 37.23), 
                    dstart = "01/01/2012", dfinish = "31/12/2012",
                    DEP = c(0, 2.5,  5,  10,  15,  20,  30,  50, 75,  100), #cm
                    minshade = 0, maxshade = 90, runshade=1,
                    scenario=2,
                   spatial = 'ncep_data/ncep_data', # it works if this line is commented out
                    terra_source='terra_climate',
                    dem.res=1000, # requested resolution DEM from elevatr in meters
                    Usrhyt = 0.01, # local height for organism
                    ERR = 1.5,
                    run.gads=2)

Error, along with general warnings/messages: 
Error in aggregate.data.frame(as.data.frame(x), ...) : arguments must have same lengthCalls: micro_ncep ... aggregate -> aggregate.default -> aggregate.data.frame

Any advice on either avoiding this error or speeding up the data download would be appreciated! Thank you again for a great R package. 
Traci DuBose

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Using terraclimate with NCEP data on a local directory
parts:
Hi Traci,

Glad you're finding the package useful!

I tried your code at my end and it ran fine. Did you put your terraclimate data in folders in the following structure within the folder you're working in?

/terra_climate/
/terra_climate_plus2c/

Also note that you shouldn't change the last depth from 200 cm unless you've got a very good reason. The model uses the last depth as a boundary condition for temperature and soil moisture, and assumes it is the mean annual temperature down there and also saturated with water. I've now put a warning in the functions about this.

All the best,
Mike

parts:
Hi Mike,

Thank you for your quick response! Sorry for my slow response; we just went through HPC maintenance, and I was hoping it might fix this problem. I am still receiving the same error after double checking the folder structure. get_terra works well on its own and within the function, and the beginning of micro_ncep works. I think the error occurs on or after line 1052. All of the packages are recently downloaded and installed in haphazard order (because of the maintenance). Could this be two packages differing in how they deal with time?  I've tried running the code with only NicheMapR loaded. I really think this is a my HPC issue; when I first started running NicheMapR on it, I had to download packages in a certain order to get it to work.

I think this might be a computer specific problem and only wanted to document for future users. I hope your projects are going well and you are having a good week so far!
Traci

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Using terraclimate with NCEP data on a local directory
parts:
Hi Traci,

One more suggestion - make sure you're running complete years because I was just alerted to an issue with the terra climate code in NicheMapR that can come up if you don't. I.e., start on 01/01/year and end on 31/12/year. I'll sort that bug out soon (it's to do with ensuring rain falls at midnight under different time zones for the soil moisture calculations - if rain falls during the day the integrator can have trouble due to the sudden change in conditions).

All the best,
Mike
